core_obligations: For an open ideal of B with inverse image I in A, show that the closure of its extension to C contains the closure of the extension of I, which is open by tautness of the composite (proof lines 1375-1379).

Choose a fundamental system of open ideals of A, let the closures of their extensions be the corresponding fundamental system of C, and take inverse images in B; verify that the closures of the extensions of those inverse images are exactly the chosen closures (proof lines 1379-1384).
Conclude that the closures of the extensions of all open ideals of B form a fundamental system of open ideals of C, that is, that the map from B to C is taut (proof lines 1384-1385).
proof_roadmap: Openness of the closure of the extension of an open ideal (proof lines 1375-1379).
The fundamental system and the conclusion (proof lines 1379-1385).
difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms from a ring A to B and from B to C, the lemma asserts that if the composite from A to C is taut then the map from B to C is taut as well (statement lines 1368-1373). The proof takes an open ideal of B and lets I be its inverse image in A; the closure of the extension of the chosen ideal contains the closure of the extension of I, which is open by tautness of the composite, so the closure of the extension of any open ideal of B is open (proof lines 1375-1379). It then shows that these closures form a fundamental system of open ideals of C: a fundamental system of open ideals of A is chosen, the closures of their extensions to C form a fundamental system by tautness of the composite, and the inverse images of those closures in B are open ideals whose extensions have exactly those closures (proof lines 1379-1385). The claim is H2: two verifications are needed -- openness of the closure of the extension of an arbitrary open ideal, and the fact that these closures cover the neighbourhoods of zero -- and both are displayed.
